text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: realtime-streaming-service p99 latency spike detected for eu-west region (>2.5s) across multiple hosts. Auto-paging to #incidents. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streams/realtime?orgId=1
oncall-amber: Seeing it — p99 and tail latency climbing. Users report stalls/reconnects. Starting quick triage.
sre-ryan: On it. First checks: kv-cache hit rate, target pool CPU utilization, recent deploys.
runtime-lee: Rolling logs for node group eu-stream-3 show a bunch of cold-starts and long scheduler wait times. KV cache hit dropped to 18% from 85% around spike.
oncall-amber: Customer-impact estimate? Maya -- can CS confirm any escalations?
customer-success-maya: Two enterprise customers (AcmeApp, BrightHealth) opened chat tickets for slow responses ~10m ago. No wide-scale customer page yet.
product-sam: Any config rollouts recently? Optimize autoscaler policy maybe changed?
sre-ryan: There was a small autoscaler tweak last night to reduce min-burst to save cost. Reverting recommended as hypothesis.
runtime-lee: Adding context: many connections are hitting cold containers because prefix-KV cache got evicted after eviction threshold bump. Trace shows tail latency concentrated on cold starts for long-context streams.
oncall-amber: Triage checklist: 1) pin traffic away from eu-stream-3 (route-shift) 2) bump min-burst on autoscaler 3) warm prefix cache 4) check deploys. Who can run route-shift?
sre-ryan: I can do route-shift to eu-stream-1 pool and enable burst capacity now. Will also raise min-burst to 4 for 10m.
runtime-lee: I'll trigger prefix-cache warmup for the affected models and users (script below).
runtime-lee: ```bash
# warm prefixes for top 100 users
for p in $(cat top_prefixes.txt); do curl -s -X POST https://eu-stream-1.internal/warm -d "{\"prefix\":\"$p\"}"; done
```
customer-success-maya: Notifying AcmeApp support contact that we're performing a route-shift and expect improvements in ~5-10m.
product-sam: Flagging this for postmortem: autoscaler min-burst change origin + cache eviction threshold interplay.
oncall-amber: Ryan — status?
sre-ryan: Route-shift executed @2824681398, min-burst bumped @2824681401, burst capacity enabled. Monitoring.
runtime-lee: Prefix warmup started @2824681406. KV hit climbing to 55% on eu-stream-1. p95 dropping from 1.2s to 450ms; p99 trending down but still elevated at ~1.6s.
oncall-amber: Good. Keep observing for 15m. If p99 > 2s after warmup, we'll escalate to full oncall bridge.
incident-bot: Pager: none paged further. Current alert status: mitigation in progress.
customer-success-maya: Customers acknowledged message, AcmeApp reported immediate improvement on sample flows.
product-sam: Also check live-retries — are we seeing client retries exacerbating tail?
sre-ryan: Retry-loop check: small bump in client retries detected immediately after spike. We've added a short backoff to the ingress proxy to smooth retries.
runtime-lee: p99 now 1.1s and still falling; p95 ~320ms. KV cache hit steady ~72%. No errors spike.
oncall-amber: Closing loop: root cause hypothesis = autoscaler min-burst reduction + eviction threshold bump caused cache churn and cold-start tail latency for streaming long sessions. Immediate mitigations: route-shift, bump min-burst, warm prefixes, proxy backoff.
product-sam: Assigning postmortem to runtime-lee + sre-ryan + product-sam. Action items: revert autoscaler change, add canary for eviction threshold, update runbook for coldstart tailspikes.
customer-success-maya: I'll follow up with impacted customers and keep CS notes updated.
sre-ryan: Marking incident as mitigated @2824681479. Will update oncall log and create incident ticket.
oncall-amber: Thanks team. Stand down in 10m unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:
